findings.title: Highscores, shared levels, player names, and telemetry use plain HTTP
findings.entry_point: Player-controlled name, level, and score values originate in ApoSimpleGame.uploadScore (ApoSimpleGame.java:962-973), while server-controlled highscore and level bytes enter through ApoHighscore.load (ApoHighscore.java:148-164) and ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.load (ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:137-153).
findings.sink: URLConnection input and output streams opened for hard-coded http:// URLs (ApoHighscore.java:81-102; ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:120-153; ApoGameCounter.java:36-55).
findings.data_path: Online operation is enabled by default at ApoConstants.java:16. ApoSimplePanel initialization starts highscore and user-level retrieval at ApoSimplePanel.java:202,205-206 and sends start telemetry containing getTextName() at ApoSimplePanel.java:227. The endpoint constants for highscore, one-button highscore, and shared levels are all HTTP at ApoConstants.java:21-28.
findings.attack_scenario: A network attacker intercepts the startup HTTP traffic, reads the player's chosen name and gameplay telemetry, then replaces get_level.php or get_highscore.php responses. The modified level data is accepted at ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:140-150 and can reach the parser and solver described in ApoSimple-02 and ApoSimple-03.
findings.preconditions: ApoConstants.B_ONLINE remains true (ApoConstants.java:16), the game can contact apo-games.de, and the attacker controls the server or a network/DNS path. Shared levels are requested automatically during initialization at ApoSimplePanel.java:205-206.
findings.validation_plan: Launch the game with a transparent or JVM HTTP proxy, allow initialization, and capture requests to get_highscore.php, get_level.php, and game_counter.php. Confirm that name/score/form data is readable without TLS, then return an altered five-line level record and verify that ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad stores it at lines 140-150.

findings.title: Short downloaded level string terminates the main game loop when selected
findings.entry_point: The first line of each five-line get_level.php record is stored unchanged at ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:140-142.
findings.sink: ApoSimpleLevel.makeLevelFromString calls substring(0, 2) 49 times without first checking the string length (ApoSimpleLevel.java:82-103).
findings.data_path: ApoSimplePanel starts loadUserlevels at ApoSimplePanel.java:205-206; ApoSimpleUserlevels.loadUserlevels retains the downloaded list at ApoSimpleUserlevels.java:32-40. Selecting Userlevels calls ApoSimplePuzzle.loadUserlevels at ApoSimplePuzzle.java:59-63, then the default UPLOAD branch constructs ApoSimpleLevel at ApoSimpleUserlevels.java:68-74, reaching the substring sink. ApoSubGame.run invokes updates without a RuntimeException catch at ApoSubGame.java:88-113.
findings.attack_scenario: A malicious server or HTTP interceptor returns one record consisting of level line "x" followed by valid metadata lines "0", "1", "1", and "0". Loading completes because the single level is not parsed during sorting. When the player selects Userlevels, substring(0, 2) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and the uncaught exception terminates the game's update thread.
findings.preconditions: The attacker can control or replace get_level.php's HTTP response, loading has completed, and the player selects the Userlevels menu.
findings.validation_plan:
Proxy get_level.php and respond with `x
0
1
1
0
`. Wait for loading, select Puzzle then Userlevels, and confirm an uncaught StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoSimpleLevel.java:87 followed by cessation of the ApoSubGame update/render loop.

findings.title: Invalid shared-level cells trigger combinatorial solver CPU exhaustion
findings.entry_point: A length-valid level string supplied by get_level.php and stored at ApoSimpleUserlevelsLoad.java:140-142.
findings.sink: The recursive search at ApoSimpleLevelSolution.java:33-94, combined with the per-candidate movement loop at lines 143-239.
findings.data_path: ApoSimpleLevel accepts every numeric two-character cell value without checking its domain at ApoSimpleLevel.java:86-97. After the selected level reaches ApoSimplePanel.setLevel at ApoSimplePanel.java:687-695, ApoSimpleLevelGame starts getMinSolution with maxSteps 4 in a new thread at ApoSimpleLevelGame.java:113-119. Unknown values qualify as candidate cells at ApoSimpleLevelSolution.java:38-49 and fall through getDirection unchanged at line 274, so each candidate can consume the 200-step guard at lines 232-238 while the recursive branch at lines 71-90 explores further candidates.
findings.attack_scenario: The attacker returns a level field made from "99" repeated 49 times plus "999" for the stars, followed by valid metadata. All 49 cells are numeric but outside the defined 0-25 domain (ApoSimpleConstants.java:366-396). Selecting the level starts a 49-way, four-move search in which invalid cells do not move or become solved, causing millions of candidate simulations and sustained CPU consumption.
findings.preconditions: The attacker controls the shared-level HTTP response or gets this record accepted by the shared server, and the player selects the malicious level. Runtime duration depends on hardware, but no early solution exists for the all-99 grid because invalid cells remain nonempty under ApoSimpleLevelSolution.java:245-249.
findings.validation_plan: Serve a five-line record whose first line is `"99" * 49 + "999"` and whose remaining lines are `0`, `1`, `1`, and `0`. Select Userlevels and record process CPU plus thread stacks. Confirmation is a solver thread remaining in ApoSimpleLevelSolution.canBeSolved/getMinSolution, repeatedly reaching the line-237 step guard; terminate the test rather than waiting for completion.

findings.title: Any completed highscore response is treated as success and grants coins
findings.entry_point: An HTTP response controlled by save_highscore.php, a network attacker, or a local cheater's proxy (ApoHighscore.java:99-105).
findings.sink: The coin balance increase in ApoSimpleGame.uploadScore at ApoSimpleGame.java:975-977.
findings.data_path: The upload button starts uploadScore at ApoSimpleGame.java:895-903. uploadScore invokes ApoHighscore.save at line 973. ApoHighscore discards every response line and returns true solely because the stream reached EOF at ApoHighscore.java:99-105; the caller then adds ADD_COINS_UPLOAD, defined as 50 at ApoSimpleConstants.java:16.
findings.attack_scenario: A local cheater routes the hard-coded HTTP endpoint through a controlled proxy, clicks Upload after reaching the score screen, and answers the POST with `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` and an empty completed body. The response loop executes zero times, save returns true, and the client grants 50 spendable hint coins even though no score was stored.
findings.preconditions: The player reaches the score-upload UI, and the attacker can answer the HTTP request. No specific response text is required; the response must merely let getInputStream complete without IOException.
findings.validation_plan: Intercept save_highscore.php with a local HTTP proxy, return status 200 with Content-Length 0, click Upload, and compare the displayed balance before and after. A 50-coin increase at ApoSimpleGame.java:977 confirms the finding.

findings.title: Editable properties file directly sets spendable coin balance
findings.entry_point: The user-editable `properties` file in the desktop process's working directory, loaded at ApoSimplePanel.java:216-220.
findings.sink: ApoSimplePanel.setCoins assigns the parsed integer and only clamps negative values at ApoSimplePanel.java:317-321; purchases trust that balance at ApoSimpleGame.java:246-264 and ApoSimpleLevelGame.java:238-244.
findings.data_path: ApoIO opens the caller-supplied fixed filename `properties` through FileInputStream at ApoIO.java:75-81 and invokes ApoSimpleProperties.readLevel at ApoIO.java:86-89. Three booleans are read first and the following unverified int is assigned as coins at ApoSimpleProperties.java:47-50. If the file ends there, ApoIO silently catches EOF at lines 88-89 after the balance has already changed.
findings.attack_scenario: A local player replaces `properties` with seven bytes `00 00 01 00 0F 42 40`: three booleans followed by the big-endian integer 1,000,000. On startup the client installs that balance, then silently accepts EOF on the next field. The player can buy hints without earning currency.
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode is used, so B_APPLET remains false (ApoConstants.java:12), and the local user can write the launch working directory.
findings.validation_plan: Close the game, preserve the original file, place the seven specified bytes in `properties` in the launch directory, and restart through ApoSimpleMain. Confirm that renderCoins displays 1000000 at ApoSimplePanel.java:897-907 and that a hint purchase succeeds through ApoSimpleGame.java:246-264.

findings.title: Local levels file supplies an unchecked negative button index
findings.entry_point: The user-editable `levels` binary file opened when the desktop player enters the level chooser (ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:50-56).
findings.data_path: ApoIO opens `levels` through FileInputStream at ApoIO.java:75-81. ApoLevelIO.readLevel accepts the file's count, level IDs, and star values without bounds checks at ApoLevelIO.java:41-46. After buttons are created, ApoSimpleLevelChooser.init calls setVisibleButtons at line 126, where the parsed level becomes a list index.
findings.attack_scenario: A malicious local file contains three big-endian integers: count 1, level 0, stars 3. Parsing succeeds, but entering the level chooser evaluates buttons.get(-1), throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException on the uncaught game loop. In-range fabricated records can likewise mark levels visible at ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:137-140.
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode is active, the attacker can place or edit `levels` in the working directory, and the player opens the level chooser.
findings.validation_plan: Create a 12-byte `levels` file containing `00 00 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 03`, start the game, and enter Puzzle then Level Chooser. Confirm IndexOutOfBoundsException from ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:139 and termination of the ApoSubGame thread.

findings.title: Dormant URLClassLoader can instantiate remote code but has no shipped call site
findings.code_excerpt: URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } );
findings.entry_point: The public constructor's path and classname parameters at ApoClassLoader.java:19-21. Repository-wide reference search found no construction or method call outside this class, so there is no shipped untrusted entry point.
findings.sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass followed by Class.newInstance at ApoClassLoader.java:69-75.
findings.data_path: The constructor stores caller-controlled path and classname at ApoClassLoader.java:19-21, getMyClass converts path to a local file URL in desktop mode or a direct URL in applet mode at lines 62-69, then loads and instantiates the named class at lines 73-75. ApoSimpleMain.java:17-32 and ApoSimpleApplet.java:39-48 do not invoke this helper.
findings.attack_scenario: This is theoretical in ApoSimple as shipped: no game UI, save parser, or network response reaches the constructor. If future integration passes an attacker URL and class name, the attacker hosts a class whose static initializer or constructor executes when getMyClass reaches lines 73-75, gaining code execution within the game's JVM permissions.
findings.preconditions: A new caller, external harness, or future clone modification must invoke ApoClassLoader with attacker-controlled parameters; that prerequisite is absent from this variant.
findings.validation_plan: To demonstrate only the dormant primitive, host a benign test class that writes a marker, set ApoConstants.B_APPLET true, construct ApoClassLoader with the test URL and class name, and call getMyClass. The marker proves loading; separately confirm that running ApoSimpleMain normally never reaches ApoClassLoader.

notes: The supplied root contains 112 Java files beneath the preserved `Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoSimple` path. No ObjectInputStream/readObject, native/System.load, process-execution, archive, XML, credential, or reachable attacker-controlled filesystem-path sink was found. ApoHelp contains an MD5 utility at ApoHelp.java:284-293, but repository-wide reference search found no caller; the actual saves have no integrity check and are classified as client_side_trust rather than weak_integrity_check. An applet entry point exists at ApoSimpleApplet.java:18,27-29, but no concrete sandbox escape or privileged sandbox assumption was demonstrated. The highscore form contains only level, points, and name at ApoHighscore.java:92-95; because server source is absent, this audit does not separately claim that arbitrary forged scores are accepted by the server.
